title: POC FastPath Convergence Check-in
summary: Weekly check-in for BlueCove POC focusing on fastpath/first-token improvements. Reviewed last week's TTFT numbers, streaming handshake variance, sequence-length profiling, and kernel hedging choices. Agreed on a targeted bench run for microburst 95th percentile and to share kernel selection matrices and bench spreadsheet.
topics: sequence length distribution and caching impact
transcript: 00:00 Lydia Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Can you hear me ok?
00:04 Maya Chen: Yeah, loud and clear. We'll kick off — we got Tomás and Ivy on as well.

00:10 Lydia Park: Great. Quick agenda: run through last week's TTFT numbers, look at streaming variance, sequence length profile, then kernel hedging decisions. Samir will walk the microbench results.
00:22 Samir Kapoor: Hey all. Quick preface, numbers are from the dedicated pool with the new prefix cache enabled, and we used the int8 quant profile for the fastpath experiments.
00:35 Tomás Rivera: Just flag — our traffic shape during peak is pretty spiky, so microbursts are our big pain point, we've seen 2x latency spikes under 30s windows.

00:45 Samir Kapoor: Yep, that's what we focused on. So median TTFT on the baseline model was about 210ms, with the tuned fastpath we saw median drop to ~95-120ms depending on sequence length and whether the KV prefix was warm.
00:59 Ivy Lin: Wait, 95 to 120ms? That's median right? What's the 95th?
01:04 Samir Kapoor: 95th sits around 380ms on the tuned path. With hedging to the conservative kernel it drops to about 320ms, but cost goes up a touch.
01:14 Maya Chen: Is that with streaming enabled or the non-streaming bench? I thought streaming added some handshake overhead for the first token.

01:21 Samir Kapoor: Good call. We ran both. Streaming handshake added about 30-40ms to TTFT when the connection had cold buffers; with keepalive and pre-warm we can shave that down to ~10-12ms. So connection management matters.
01:35 Tomás Rivera: Our current infra uses short-lived worker pods which might kill the pre-warm, so that could explain the spikes.
01:40 Lydia Park: Right, one of the recommendations is to use a short pre-warm pool or sticky routing for high qps endpoints so the prefix cache stays hot.
01:50 Maya Chen: Can you explain the kernel hedging a bit more — what do you mean by 'conservative kernel'?

01:55 Samir Kapoor: Sure. We have a lower-latency, aggressive kernel optimized for shorter sequences and single-token throughput, but its variance is higher on long sequences. The conservative kernel trades a bit more median RTT for reduced variance. Hedging means we try the aggressive path first, and if the response doesn't start within a threshold we route to conservative as a fallback.
02:14 Ivy Lin: Does hedging double cost? How do we avoid paying for two executions?
02:18 Samir Kapoor: We send lightweight probe or use early-signal heuristics — we don't fully execute two heavy runs. In practice cost uplift was 5-12% in our bench, depending on the probe threshold.
02:29 Tomás Rivera: Ok that range is acceptable. What about sequence length — we run a lot of 2k to 8k sequences for summarization. How does that shift the fastpath gains?

02:38 Samir Kapoor: The fastpath is most effective under 2k; beyond ~3k the kernel switching favors conservative due to memory movement. For 4k–8k, median TTFT was closer to 160–240ms tuned, 95th up to 520ms if the KV cache was cold.
02:52 Maya Chen: So the prefix cache heat is huge. Any strategy for maintaining it with our usage pattern?

02:57 Samir Kapoor: We suggested two things: short-lived sticky routing for heavy endpoints and opportunistic prefetching for top-k prompt prefixes. Also adjusting autoscaler to keep a small standby of warmed workers.
03:10 Lydia Park: Also note the cache TTL we used was 4 minutes in the bench — can increase if you have predictable repeated prefixes.
03:17 Maya Chen: Hmm probably ok to bump TTL for certain endpoints. Next, Samir, can you walk the microburst sample from Tuesday?

03:24 Samir Kapoor: Yeah. We replayed a 10-minute trace with 800 qps bursts — the key takeaway: bursts where >30% requests arrive within 10s window caused queueing on the GPU scheduler. Our mitigation experiments were: smaller batch windows with priority queueing for first-token, and pipeline shedding for non-critical background calls.
03:40 Tomás Rivera: Does priority queueing hurt throughput for full-sequence jobs?
03:43 Samir Kapoor: Slightly — about 3–5% throughput loss during sustained bursts, but TTFT 95th improved by ~120–150ms for prioritized calls.
03:50 Ivy Lin: Can we apply priority only to our authentication endpoints and critical user-facing routes?
03:54 Lydia Park: Yes that's the typical pattern. Redwood Console lets you set per-route priority weights and tie those to SLAs.
04:02 Maya Chen: On the subject of quantization — you said int8 for the fastpath bench. Any regrets vs int4?

04:08 Samir Kapoor: int4 reduces memory but increases kernel instability for some ops and unpredictability for long KV caches; int8 hit a good sweet spot for stability and latency. We can run an int4-only bench if you want to push cost further but expect some quality/regressions.
04:22 Tomás Rivera: We'll probably require int8 for initial pilot, fine to revisit int4 if cost targets require.
04:26 Lydia Park: Quick interjection — Maya, earlier you asked about 95th, do you have an SLO for that threshold?
04:31 Maya Chen: We want 95th under 350ms for core query endpoints, ideally 250ms but that's optimistic.

04:36 Samir Kapoor: With sticky routing + prefix TTL bump + hedging to conservative kernel we're pretty confident we can hit ~320ms 95th in the pilot for most sequences under 2k. For 4k+ sequences it's harder, we'd aim for 400ms–450ms.
04:48 Maya Chen: That seems reasonable. Anything else in the sample tests?

04:51 Samir Kapoor: One more: streaming partial-output optimization. We implemented an early-output path that emits initial token bytes before full attention recompute for the chunk; that reduced first-byte latency by ~40ms for long-streaming sessions.
05:03 Tomás Rivera: But does that affect token continuity or hallucination risk?
05:08 Samir Kapoor: Slightly — it's a tradeoff. We keep a high-precision fallback for tokens flagged as risky by our heuristic.
05:14 Ivy Lin: Ok, I'd like to see the failure cases for that — can you annotate examples in the bench sheet?
05:19 Samir Kapoor: Yes, we'll annotate the flagged examples and push to the shared spreadsheet.
05:23 Lydia Park: Quick housekeeping — we added a short recording of the bench commands and the config used to reproduce runs; link at the end.
05:30 Maya Chen: Perfect. Now, security/compliance check — any config changes that touch tenancy or data flows?

05:35 Samir Kapoor: No tenant changes. Fastpath and hedging are routing/exec decisions inside the runtime. For Dedicated we keep data in your VPC and logs are optional. We can turn off any telemetry you don't want.
05:46 Ivy Lin: Good. Can you confirm KMS integration for our artifacts?
05:50 Lydia Park: Yes — Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration. We'll share the integration guide.
05:56 Tomás Rivera: Great. Back to numbers: do you have a recommended probe threshold for hedging?

06:01 Samir Kapoor: In our benches 120ms probe threshold gave the best tradeoff for your traffic shape; with 80ms you hedge too aggressively and cost rises, with 200ms you lose most of the 95th improvements.
06:13 Maya Chen: 120ms sounds fine. We'll want to tune in staging though.
06:17 Lydia Park: For staging we can provision a small dedicated pool to run the hedging experiments without affecting prod.
06:22 Tomás Rivera: That would be ideal. Also, can you produce a config diff we can drop into our infra-as-code for autoscaler changes?
06:28 Samir Kapoor: Yep we'll put together a sample HCL snippet for the autoscaler, sticky routing, and cache TTL adjustments.
06:34 Maya Chen: Awesome. Anything on model version pinning? We've noticed different models have different kernel performance.
06:39 Samir Kapoor: Pinning to a verified model build is best for consistency. We can maintain a model catalog entry with recommended quant/kernel profile per model.
06:46 Ivy Lin: Will Redwood provide regression alerts if a model upgrade regresses TTFT?
06:50 Lydia Park: Yes, Redwood Optimize can tie prompt-based evals to releases and send regression alerts.
06:55 Maya Chen: Ok good to know. Let's talk next steps and concrete bench runs — Maya?

07:00 Maya Chen: We want: (1) microburst 95th run with our 10-minute trace and stalled worker behavior, (2) 4k and 8k sequence benches with cold-vs-warm prefix cache, (3) streaming early-token failure cases annotated. Target completion by end of next week.
07:15 Lydia Park: Good. Samir will own the bench artifacts and share the spreadsheet. Action items after the recap.
07:22 Samir Kapoor: One note: we'll include a kernel decision matrix that lists which kernel we recommend by seqlen bucket and quant profile.
07:30 Tomás Rivera: Will you also include cost delta estimates?
07:33 Samir Kapoor: Yes — cost delta per 100k tokens and per-hour reserved pool estimates.
07:38 Maya Chen: We might ask for an int4 spot test afterwards if the cost estimates still push us over budget.
07:44 Lydia Park: Fair. For security docs I'll share the Private deployment KMS guide and audit log options.
07:50 Ivy Lin: Can we also set a follow-up call after the bench results? Preferably with the SREs and a couple engineers so we can go over configs.
07:57 Lydia Park: Yes let's do a deep-dive next Thursday same time. I'll send a calendar invite pending availability.
08:03 Maya Chen: Great. Anything else from the Redwood side?
08:06 Samir Kapoor: We'll also drop the scripts we used to generate the replay and the flame graphs for the GPU scheduler hotspots.
08:13 Tomás Rivera: That will be super helpful.
08:16 Lydia Park: Ok recap and action items coming up now.

08:20 Lydia Park: Recap: baseline vs tuned median TTFT improved to ~95-120ms for short sequences, 95th improved with hedging but still sensitive to cold prefix cache; streaming handshake can be minimized with keepalives; microburst priority queueing yields TTFT gains with small throughput cost. Agreed bench runs and artifacts to be shared.
08:42 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll look out for the spreadsheet and invite for the follow-up deep-dive.
08:46 Lydia Park: Thanks all, talk soon. Bye.
08:48 [meeting ended]
